inspection_coverage.note: Every required pair in this W3 scope is represented. UNDERDETERMINED is deliberate fail-closed output, not evidence of independence.

pair_adjudications.rationale: ACT-R trace/activation/retrieval operators differ from beta-VAE latent rate-distortion encoding/reconstruction. No source-explicit shared model ancestor was established.
ACT-R declarative traces and activation-based retrieval differ from simultaneous population superposition plus cue-conditioned Bayesian recall.
Declarative-memory retrieval/decay is structurally distinct from Bayesian reward-structure belief updating and belief-state action selection.

Both use past information to condition current inference/retrieval, but ACT-R retrieval activation and HMM latent-state inference are different source-native mechanisms with no explicit shared model ancestry.
ACT-R declarative memory operators differ from continuous forward/inverse motor internal-model learning.
ACT-R declarative trace/retrieval mechanics differ from SORN recurrent neural plasticity and supervised motor readout.
Both contain a memory-like retained quantity, but ACT-R stores declarative traces while SKL-03 caches one last successful aim; this shared retention constituent is not shared genealogy.
Semantic beta-VAE compression of episodes differs from noisy population-code superposition and posterior recall in visual short-term memory.
Both employ probabilistic latent/belief representations, but beta-VAE rate-distortion compression and Bayesian RL structure belief are different operators.
Both use latent probabilistic representations; VAE compression/reconstruction and HMM state filtering are different source-native mechanisms without explicit common ancestry.
Latent generative compression is distinct from synergy-factorized forward/inverse motor learning.
Beta-VAE semantic compression is distinct from SORN recurrent STDP/IP/SN plasticity.
Semantic rate-distortion compression is distinct from reinforcement-gated cached-aim updating and local motor exploration.
Both use probabilistic inference, but palimpsest storage/recall and Bayesian reward-structure learning have different modeled states and updates.
Both perform probabilistic inference from noisy evidence, but population-memory posterior recall and HMM latent-state filtering are not source-supported as one model family.
Population superposition memory differs from forward/inverse internal motor-model learning.
Visual short-term palimpsest storage differs from recurrent SORN sequence plasticity.
Population-code memory storage/retrieval differs from cached motor aim plus outcome-dependent exploration.
Both are probabilistic state/belief models for sequential behavior, but PRD-02 learns uncertainty over reward-generation structure while PRD-03 filters latent trial state with an HMM/B matrix.
Bayesian reward-structure learning/action selection differs from gradient-based forward/inverse motor learning.
Bayesian RL structure belief differs from SORN neural sequence plasticity.
Both concern exploration/action selection under reward, but PRD-02 performs Bayesian structural belief planning whereas SKL-03 uses local variability and last-success aim caching.
HMM latent trial-state inference differs from continuous forward/inverse motor learning.
HMM evidence integration differs from recurrent STDP/IP/SN sequence-learning dynamics.
Latent-state world-model inference differs from local reinforcement-gated motor aim update.
Forward/inverse internal-model gradient learning differs from SORN recurrent neural plasticity, despite common motor-learning explananda.
Both contain exploration/noise in motor learning, but SKL-01 learns forward/inverse internal models while SKL-03 updates a single cached aim from reinforcement.
SORN recurrent plasticity and supervised motor readout differ from phenomenological last-success aim caching and outcome-dependent exploration.
